transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-14 09:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Liam, Rina (Redwood) --- Priya, Samir, Evan, Olga (Horizon)

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining us. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood side, and I have Liam and Rina here to run through the hosted embeddings and rerank demo.
[00:00:12] Priya Kapoor: Hi Maya, thanks. Quick context: we're redoing search across our ecommerce catalog. Current infra is a homegrown vector index backed by FAISS and we use an in-house small reranker. Latency target is under 150ms p95. Cost is also a hard constraint.
[00:00:25] Liam Ortiz: Got it. We'll show how Redwood's hosted embeddings + rerank flow works, typical latencies, and cost levers. We can also show the Console traces and Optimize suggestions for batching.
[00:00:40] Samir Patel: Quick note, security is super important. We need SAML SSO and audit logs, and possible VPC access later.
[00:00:47] Rina Das: Absolutely. We have SOC2 and ISO docs, and for Private we can offer VPC and on-prem packaged flow. We'll share links after.
[00:01:05] Evan Reyes: Also curious about competitor tradeoffs — we've chatted with Pinecone and looked at OpenAI embeddings.
[00:01:12] Maya Chen: Totally. We'll call out where Redwood differs especially on unit economics and rerank integration.

-- Demo start --
[00:02:10] Liam Ortiz: Alright, I'm sharing my screen. First, the flow. Step one: embeddings API to vectorize user queries and docs. Step two: fast approximate retrieval (customer index) then Redwood's hosted rerank endpoint which takes query + top-K and returns reranked results or scores.
[00:02:33] Liam Ortiz: Example request: POST /v1/embeddings -> vector; then POST /v1/rerank with query embedding and candidates. We support streaming scores and structured output for labels.
[00:02:50] Olga Smirnov: Is the rerank executed on the same runtime as generation or different? We worry about cold starts.
[00:02:57] Rina Das: Rerank uses a lightweight MLP or small transformer variant optimized for low latency on our serving runtime. It's placed on a different pool when you pin a rerank model to a dedicated instance. Hosted has warm pools with autoscaling.
[00:03:18] Priya Kapoor: What about KV cache — does that help rerank?
[00:03:23] Liam Ortiz: KV cache is mostly for autoregressive generation. For rerank we use prefix caching of embeddings and a small in-memory candidate cache. Sorry sometimes transcription shows KV cash.
[00:03:40] Samir Patel: Haha, KV cash indeed.

[00:04:05] Liam Ortiz: Now, latency examples from our benchmarks: for a 5-candidate rerank on T4-class hosted pool, p50 ~28ms, p95 ~95ms depending on seq length of the reranker. For larger Bfloat models numbers go up. We also show how batching affects latency and token cost.
[00:04:31] Priya Kapoor: Those numbers look promising. Our query patterns are short — usually 8-20 tokens.
[00:04:40] Liam Ortiz: Great. Also show Console: trace view for a rerank request with token-level cost breakdown. The Console's Optimize module recommended a 16-batch window for your qps profile and showed estimated monthly token spend.
[00:05:05] Evan Reyes: Can you demo how Optimize suggests quantization? We've been cautious about quality regression.
[00:05:12] Rina Das: Sure. Optimize runs evals on your sample prompt set. It suggests quantization profiles per model; e.g., INT8 for baseline models with expected <1% relevance regression. It surfaces eval metrics and example mismatches so you can decide.
[00:05:36] Samir Patel: Do you support on-the-fly fallbacks if a quantized model misbehaves in production?
[00:05:41] Liam Ortiz: Yes, rollout policies can define automatic fallback to a full-precision variant if quality drops beyond thresholds.

[00:06:15] Priya Kapoor: For the pilot, we need to know how to run A/B — current vs Redwood rerank for a slice of traffic.
[00:06:23] Maya Chen: We can do canary routing in the Console. You define a percentage, and Console shows per-route model metrics, for relevance and latency. We'll include an example canary config in the pilot doc.

[00:07:00] Liam Ortiz: Switching to a live example: I have a demo index with product descriptions. I'm sending a query "wireless over ear headphones". We'll get top-50 from index then rerank top-10.
[00:07:20] [00:07:20] Speaker 1: (transcription artifact) um uh so the results are returning, first pass...
[00:07:28] Liam Ortiz: The rerank response includes scores and an explanation field if you enable structured output. See the latency 34ms here.
[00:07:36] Samir Patel: I see the explanation but some of the tokenization is off in the snippet. Is that from the index side?
[00:07:42] Rina Das: Likely index snippets; we truncate at sentence boundaries but we can customize.

[00:08:15] Priya Kapoor: On cost — can you show an example cost per 1000 queries for embedding + rerank?
[00:08:21] Liam Ortiz: Yes. Rough ballpark: embedding vectorize ~0.6 USD per 1k for 1536-d embeddings on hosted baseline, rerank ~1.8 USD per 1k for small transformer. With batching and caching you can reduce effective cost by ~30-40% for repetitive prefixes. We'll send a detailed calc.
[00:08:45] Priya Kapoor: That aligns with our target if we can keep p95 under 150ms.

[00:09:10] Olga Smirnov: For data residency, can we pin region and ensure logs are retained only per our policy?
[00:09:16] Maya Chen: Yes. Hosted can pin requests to region; audit logs and retention are configurable. For stricter needs we recommend Redwood Private.

[00:09:45] Evan Reyes: You mentioned fallback to cheaper models — how does routing decide when to use fallback?
[00:09:50] Liam Ortiz: Routing policies can be based on capacity (if primary pool overloaded), latency SLO breaches, or custom heuristics like cost caps. You can set automatic fallback to a quantized or smaller-model variant.

[00:10:20] Samir Patel: Any limits on top-K size for rerank? We sometimes run K=50.
[00:10:26] Rina Das: We support larger K but note cost scales linearly with K for the rerank step. Some customers do approximate prefiltering to keep K smaller. We also have a chunked rerank mode that pipelines candidates to stay within latency SLO.

[00:11:05] Priya Kapoor: Let's talk success metrics for the pilot. We want: relevance uplift >5% NDCG@10 and p95 latency <150ms, cost per query under $0.05.
[00:11:16] Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable. We'll include those as the pilot's goals.

[00:11:40] Liam Ortiz: Back to Console: the Trace view includes per-token timing, route selection, and a heatmap of batch sizes used. The Optimize suggestions flagged that your traffic pattern with peek hours at 11am PT benefits from small bursts and a slightly larger baseline pool.
[00:12:05] Priya Kapoor: For the pilot dataset, we'll share around 20k queries and a 100k doc subset. Samir will send that.

[00:12:30] Samir Patel: Quick question: do you provide embeddings-only endpoints to push docs in bulk? We currently bulk compute and upsert.
[00:12:36] Liam Ortiz: Yes, bulk embeddings endpoints with async job status are supported. We return job ids and allow parallel workers for throughput. There is also an upload SDK we can share.

[00:13:10] [00:13:10] Speaker 2: minor audio glitch, bridging call...

[00:13:40] Rina Das: On security: SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC, KMS integration for customer-managed keys — all supported. For audit logs, Console exposes per-route logs and download.
[00:14:05] Olga Smirnov: KMS — does it integrate with our existing HSM?
[00:14:09] Maya Chen: We support AWS KMS and customer HSM integrations for Private deployments; for hosted there are options for BYOK via KMS.

[00:14:40] Priya Kapoor: Any vendor lock-in concerns? If we start hosted and want to move to Private, how seamless is the model/versioning?
[00:14:48] Liam Ortiz: We try to keep the API and model indexing consistent. You can pin exact model versions and our deployment abstraction is designed to let you migrate with minimal code changes. There are infra differences but the same routes and rollout configs remain.

[00:15:25] Evan Reyes: Are there any reference customers with similar scale we can talk to?
[00:15:29] Maya Chen: Yes, we can make intros to a couple of retail customers doing rerank pilots — I'll include that in the follow-up.

-- Technical deep dive highlights (later in call) --
[00:22:00] Liam Ortiz: For the SE deep part, we discussed kernel selection: runtime picks kernels by model arch and sequence distribution. For short seq rerank tasks we optimize attention kernels to reduce memory bandwidth. There's an auto-batching layer that groups small requests within a 10-20ms window to maximize GPU util.
[00:22:30] Samir Patel: Does auto-batching affect p50 significantly?
[00:22:35] Liam Ortiz: Slightly increases p50 for low QPS, but reduces p95 and overall cost. Optimize sim shows tradeoffs per your QPS shape.

[00:28:10] Priya Kapoor: One edge: we need deterministic rerank for some audits — can Redwood ensure deterministic outputs across runs?
[00:28:18] Rina Das: Determinism depends on model choice and sampling settings. For rerank we use score outputs and deterministic models, you can set seed and disable sampling to get deterministic rankings.

[00:33:00] Maya Chen: Quick recap before we wrap: Horizon wants to run a 2-week pilot, objectives NDCG@10 + latency + cost cap. Redwood will send pricing and security docs, SE to run bench test with their corpus.
[00:33:25] Priya Kapoor: Perfect. Also please include an example canary config and rollback policy.
[00:33:31] Rina Das: Will do.

[00:34:00] Evan Reyes: Any gotchas we should be aware of when migrating from FAISS to your flow?
[00:34:06] Liam Ortiz: Main ones: vector dimension mismatches, index sharding patterns, and ensuring your prefilter retrieves high-recall top-K. We can help tune the prefilter and sampling set for evals.

[00:36:20] Samir Patel: For benchmarking, can Redwood run an on-demand bench with our queries and hardware sim?
[00:36:25] Liam Ortiz: Yes, we offer bench tests as part of pilot — we'll need sample queries and target SLOs.

[00:40:00] [00:40:00] Speaker 3: brief crosstalk

[00:41:10] Priya Kapoor: Final question — SLA for hosted?
[00:41:15] Maya Chen: Hosted has best-effort SLOs; Dedicated and Private have SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers. For pilot we recommend hosted or a small dedicated pool depending on desired guarantees.

[00:44:00] Liam Ortiz: Okay sending the pilot config doc now in chat (link stub: https://redwood.example/pilot-horizon). We'll include cost calc and example API calls.

[00:45:10] Priya Kapoor: Thanks — we'll review and aim to have Samir's data over by Monday.

[00:50:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with pricing, SOC2, and schedule the bench next Tuesday.
[00:50:10] Priya Kapoor: Appreciate it.

End of transcript.
